feature: ADR-0084 Linux main-thread signalfd and child mask restoration

linux.abi: signalfd_siginfo size128/signo offset0/flags/native prototypes checked; no signal or device calls in oracle

windows.scope: Linux-only change; earlier native/portable pending checks remain after automatic approval quota failure

limitations: Native own-process signals only; no foreground-group signal, native terminal Ctrl+C, VT, evdev/uinput, Hook/SendInput or driver operations.
Installer requires sole actual main thread, default dispositions and initially unblocked managed signals. /proc task check is a snapshot; caller must prevent concurrent thread creation.
Later threads inherit blocked signals and must never unblock them; owner is !Send/Sync. No generic multithreaded embedding support.
Child Command must be prepared while owner lives and trusted hooks must not alter restored mask/group/session.
Close restores previous mask and may deliver a concurrently arriving pending signal with its default disposition; explicit close only after actual child exit/cleanup. Drop is best effort.
Host Supervisor lifecycle/run-linux CLI remain unconnected; signal receipt is not Stop delivery, actual exit, progress or input recovery.
